thread:
alex.cheng: quick heads-up — during the weekly encryption audit I found ~15 snapshots in s3://rwd-prod-backups that are NOT SSE-KMS. looks like a mix of RDS snapshots exported to S3 and some object-store dumps.
maya_g: ouch. any idea timeframe/which backups?
alex.cheng: entries from 2025-11-12 -> 2026-02-03. examples: backups/2026-01-05/pg-dump.sql (no SSE), rds-exports/2026-01-20/export.tar (no sse).
samir: do we have a detection rule firing? shouldn't we have a bucket policy deny for non-SSE?
ops-bot: alert: s3-unencrypted-object-detect fired for s3://rwd-prod-backups on 2026-02-03T11:22Z (count:1)
alex.cheng: detection exists but it looks like IAM changes allowed a CI job to put without SSE last quarter. need short-term containment + long-term policy + KMS RBAC tightening.
security-oncall: propose immediate actions: 1) block public/read access 2) add bucket policy deny PutObject if x-amz-server-side-encryption != "aws:kms" 3) identify all principals that did PutObject without SSE -> revoke immediate 4) schedule re-encrypt job for objects and RDS exports.
jordan_k: note: RDS snapshots can't be encrypted in-place. for any unencrypted RDS snapshot we need to restore to an encrypted instance or export and re-import into encrypted instance. DB team FYI.
maya_g: i'll take the re-encrypt job for S3 objects. plan: copy objects to same key with aws s3 cp + --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id <new-cmk>, then delete originals. will run in batches and validate checksums.
samir: i'll prepare a scoped KMS policy. idea: separate CMKs per environment and restrict Decrypt to a small list of roles (restore-runner, rds-restore, dataplane-service). also require condition aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn for lambdas/ecs tasks. example IAM snippet:```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/restore-runner"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": {"aws:SourceAccount": "123456789012"},
        "ArnLike": {"aws:SourceArn": "arn:aws:lambda:us-west-2:123456789012:function:restore-*"}
      }
    }
  ]
}```
maya_g: good. also add CloudTrail Data Events for S3 + KMS CloudTrail events to the audit trail. we need decrypt events to be surfaced in SIEM.
alex.cheng: agree. add CloudWatch metric filter on CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt and s3:PutObject without sse to create PagerDuty alerts.
pd-bot: pagerduty incident created: INC-20260320-042, severity: medium — unencrypted backups found
security-oncall: vuln triage: is this CVE-level? probably not a CVE but a control failure. however treat as moderate security incident: data at rest protection gap. we should run a scope review: which customer data exposures could exist if these snapshots were exfiltrated.
jordan_k: I'll trigger the customer-data-scope job and list snapshots with PII tags.
samir: bucket policy deny example to push asap:```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "DenyUnEncryptedUploads",
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": "s3:PutObject",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::rwd-prod-backups/*",
      "Condition": {
        "StringNotEquals": {"s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms"}
      }
    }
  ]
}```
alex.cheng: additional containment: rotate the CMK used for the affected objects? if we rotate we need to ensure old ciphertext can still be decrypted until re-encryption finished. maybe create a NEW CMK and use it for re-encryption then schedule key disable/rotate for the old one.
maya_g: correct. re-encrypt to new CMK, validate, then schedule disable of old CMK after 30 days. need a playbook for that.
security-oncall: incident response steps to record in runbook: 1) identify unencrypted artifacts 2) contain (bucket policy, revoke principals) 3) re-encrypt/copy to new CMK or restore+recreate for RDS 4) update RBAC and KMS policies 5) enable audit logs & alerts 6) communicate to legal/compliance if customer data present 7) post-incident review and SLA credit decision if needed.
jordan_k: how about automatic remediation moving forward? lambda triggered on PutObject that rewrites object with correct SSE and tags it as "re-encrypted-by". low risk but need to ensure no recursion loops.
samir: implement put-object check: if header missing, copy object to same key with SSE and then delete original. ensure Lambda has kms:Encrypt & s3:PutObject allowed.
alex.cheng: quick question on KMS RBAC: do we limit kms:Decrypt to role only or also to users? prefer role-only for automation and require human ops to assume role for manual restores.
security-oncall: agree — role-only decrypt is safer. add an emergency key escrow procedure for legal/forensic need that requires approval by security lead + one exec. record in key access log.
maya_g: running first re-encrypt batch now (prefix backups/2026-01/). will post progress.
ops-bot: runbook:encryption-incident started by alex.cheng at 2026-03-20T09:14Z
ops-bot: s3-copy-job started batch 1 (100 objects)
maya_g: batch 1 done, 0 mismatches, will continue next batch in 10m.
alex.cheng: samir/maya please update internal runbook doc and add the bucket policy to infra repo as an emergency PR. tag me and security-oncall.
samir: on it. opening PR now.
jordan_k: scope job returned 3 snapshots with PII flag, pinging legal/compliance and cust-safety.
security-oncall: thanks. once re-encrypt finished we'll close the incident and run a postmortem. for now assign owners: maya=re-encrypt, samir=KMS/RBAC & bucket policy, jordan=scope/customer contact, alex=incident lead.
alex.cheng: thanks team. quick wins first (deny policy + revoke) then re-encrypt. :thumbsup:
maya_g: done with batch 2 as well, ETA full run 90m.
ops-bot: runbook update: batch 3 failure (transient 5xx) — retry scheduled
security-oncall: logging note — ensure CloudTrail log file validation is turned on for the bucket where trail writes.
alex.cheng: will follow up. closing updates here once all batches done and PR merged. keep pagerduty incident open until verification.
pd-bot: incident INC-20260320-042 updated: status=investigating, assignees=[alex.cheng, maya_g, samir]
maya_g: 11:40 - all S3 objects re-encrypted. starting validations and tagging.
alex.cheng: confirmed tags present and CMK is new-key-2026. samir, please proceed to update KMS policy to restrict Decrypt as discussed.
samir: policy PR merged, IAM changes deployed, CloudTrail filter for kms:Decrypt created.
security-oncall: incident resolved; will schedule 1-week follow-up postmortem. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
